headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is also elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents and session memory, while Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP servers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if A’s outputs are fed into B’s tools or prompts. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or MCP tool inputs
IF agent_b treats file contents from a shared workspace as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts
Add a strict delimiter/template around any transferred text
Require human review before MCP tool calls that consume agent_a content
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches personal and finance data and has allowlisted network egress; agent_b has broad egress, reads/writes filesystem, and handles plugin credentials. If they share files or context, sensitive data can flow from A into B and then out through B’s network path. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a stores customer or finance data in files readable by agent_b
IF agent_b forwards shared context or file contents to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep agent_a data in a separate directory with restrictive ACLs
Disable file sharing between the agents
Rotate any plugin credentials exposed to agent_b
Review outbound destinations for agent_b before enabling it
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on handoff paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances with session memory, and agent_b supports multiple instances with per-kernel state plus shared memory store. Both can write to filesystem-like surfaces, so concurrent mutation conflicts are plausible even though agent_a’s write surface is less explicit. Uncertainty about A’s writable surfaces escalates this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or memory store
IF concurrent runs modify shared artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid shared memory-store namespaces
Check in-progress files before overwriting
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while agent_b is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or persisted state. Because B can execute tool-driven workflows, the blast radius is larger than a simple misparse.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as direct inputs to plugins or agents
IF no verification step checks A’s facts before B acts on them
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking tool call
Require citations or source links for A-generated claims
Limit B to read-only evaluation of A outputs
Log and review any automated downstream actions
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and rollback for actions

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b handles plugin credentials and broad external APIs. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention, residency, and third-party processing, even though no specific jurisdiction is documented. The lack of explicit controls means medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is routed through agent_b plugins or external model providers
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Map which regulated data classes each agent may touch
Block regulated data from agent_b plugins unless approved
Document retention and deletion settings for both agents
Review residency of external API endpoints
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for data-class routing
